w: Two coordinate posts for blacking the spot are directions (T3-070, both readers); a VPN or proxy sought to beat the timer and 'Switch accounts' given as the answer place beyond the limit (T3-088, reader B and my B1).

Both readers placed T3-070. Four concepts report the Monado placed and its state: 'We are making a monado', the move confirmed 'at 897,503', pixels added there, 'Blade shape is done' and a border begun (T3-038, my B1); T3-038's discriminator against T3-070 puts coordinates of the work in progress with T3-038. Three calls to help build it and write 'I'm Really Feeling It' are T3-002, fewer than T3-038's four; the hilt's and the I's starting coordinates are directions (T3-070).

q: Whose eyes find the mark: the room's own members finding work they did not know of go to T3-082; outsiders led to the sub go to T3-044.
w: 'Didn't know there was a Devon subreddit until I saw this' is someone of Devon led to the sub by its flag: new to the sub (T3-044, my B1) but no outsider to the county, which reader A read as members finding their mark (T3-082). The test names only members and outsiders. 'Link?' answered with the canvas link points to the standing flag, T3-026 by T3-070's discriminator against T3-038, not a direction (T3-070, reader B and my B1).

q: Are directions shared for use (T3-070), or one plan imposed against others (T3-091)?
w: A screenshot suggested as the guide, reference images collected, colours coordinated, and the image posted 'so people over here would be using the exact same image' share one picture for use. No rival version is named and no stray corrected, so the boundary ruled once gives T3-070 (reader A, my B1), not T3-091 (reader B). Talk kept in the existing thread, a colour thread started and new threads discouraged gather it (T3-015, named by neither reader).

A revised template published, the change announced, a gridded image and 'USE DARK GREEN' are directions posted (T3-070, reader A); helpers told to use the template because others keep fixing their work, defenders told to stop erasing allied blue, and fixers who mess up the eyes are strays corrected (T3-091, reader B). The boundary ruled once puts each act on its side, as my B1 had. A timer glitch explained, refreshing before each pixel and a newcomer taught to pick a colour and place are T3-016's 'how to pick a colour and place' (named by neither reader; the correction on teaching to place).

q: Coordinates, templates, grid images, overlays, guides, colour plans, border plans, timings or how-to posted or updated for placers to follow by hand.
w: Three of five concepts ask what to call the blue line between the corners and propose 'the Beam'. No theme's test holds naming a feature of the faction's ground: T3-070 (reader A) lists directions, and T3-091 (reader B) needs one plan imposed against others. The sign plan and the call to make the sign a link 'so people come here and coordinate' are one concept each, T3-004 or T3-169 against T3-044 (my B1 had T3-004 and T3-169).

The official coordination and plan declared, a posted copy called 24 hours old, and 'Houd je aan het plan' hold placers to one plan (T3-091, both readers); two 'Huidig plan' updates and 'do not expand the flag, fill the left with orange' are a plan updated and directions (T3-070, reader B). The boundary ruled once splits them so. My B1 T3-042 rests on a fill order and an upgrade, not upkeep chosen over growth.

Thirty-one concepts name a target to destroy: the OSU logo, the Mona Lisa, the Plagueis copypasta, the PC Master Race logo, No Step on Snek, and the American, British, Welsh, Swiss, Swedish and Mexican flags ('destroy this filthy flag'). By T3-171's decide_when_both a named target makes these T3-006, placed by neither reader (reader B listed it under also_present). Fourteen more themes have three concepts of their own: black spread for its own sake, 'complete consumption of all' (T3-171); effort narrowed to one core or target (T3-069, my B1); new core spots (T3-020); polls (T3-066); timed attacks (T3-167); roles (T3-103); a situation-room thread (T3-015); complaints of no organisation (T3-049); coordinates (T3-070); questions where to help (T3-034); rallies (T3-002); current plans and orders (T3-091, reader A); truces with Germany and r/placehearts (T3-149); alliances (T3-150).

Twenty-one concepts have the road ruling on other rooms' requests to build: the recognised-art list, approvals asked and given, 'Sorry, that intersection is protected', 'We're not approving art at this time' (T3-162, reader B and my B1). Eighteen declare the current project or plan and tell placers to follow it, 'Current Project: Yoshi Kart', 'OFFICIAL ANNOUNCEMENT', building guidelines (T3-091, both readers). Five name one piece the priority, the bounce colours, the sign, the title, He-Man (T3-069), and four refuse new work to hold what the road has: too few online for Blue's push, a moratorium on new core art, no karts for now, Void defence before the banana (T3-042). Four themes with three concepts of their own: a bag.

Eleven concepts repair the work: the flag at 913,465 cleaned, the Queen's and Willem's faces restored from vandals, a synchronised fix of A to O celebrated (T3-021, reader B). Seven name placers on a 'muur der schaamte' and ask them to stop, with proof demanded before release; c0035 calls them 'Spanjaarden' who do not know the anthem (T3-008, named by neither reader; my B1 had T3-121, but no one is banned or excluded). Four hold builders to the anthem's official spelling and the plan (T3-091, both readers), and three name 'saboteurs' and a user said to keep painting 578,6 orange (T3-087, my B1). Four themes with three concepts of their own: a bag.

'having two links is causing some confusion ... were fighting ourselves', 'I'm not sure how to start coordinating this' and 'has anyone laid down tiles?' complain of scattered calls (T3-049, reader B); a new template made and everyone told to follow it is the remedy (T3-091, both readers, my B1). By T3-049's decide_when_both the act leads only with more concepts; it has fewer, so T3-049 is primary.

Both readers placed T3-091. The 'more prominent' numbers started at (709,603) are a second piece, not a rival design of the first; 'We already have the numbers ... you could help us maintain them' drops it for the piece already standing, which T3-091's discriminator against T3-069 gives to T3-069 (my B1).

'stick to the original lettering', fending off fixers who change the template, and asking whether the relocation is now the plan hold placers to one plan (T3-091, both readers, my B1); one thread made for all logo talk and used for the game plan gathers it (T3-015, reader A; reader B listed it under also_present). Reader B's bag falls short: T3-049 keeps two concepts of its own once the call for one thread goes to T3-015, and T3-005 two once 'STOP DESTROYING THE MUSHROOM', which reins in the room's own placers, is set aside.

Both readers placed T3-091: members plead to get 'on the same page', message those undoing the redesign, and ask others to stop fighting each other. Five concepts also cut the design down to the hands: stopping at 'TENN', not past the second N, falling back to the T, 'a real power T only', 'smaller and easier to defend' (T3-069's 'a design scaled down to fit the hands', my B1). My B1 T3-004 and T3-170 drop: the scaling is T3-069's, and the undoing is members disagreeing, not friendly work taken for vandalism.

Fourteen concepts put holding, cleaning and defending before expansion: 'This should take precedence over expansion', 'Better to be neat than a red blob', the hammer and sickle protected 'during this fascist brigade' before any offensive, the expansion plan cancelled for 'defense and void countering' (T3-042, named by neither reader). Operations and an official endgame declared (T3-091, both readers), the hammer and sickle made the one piece to watch (T3-069, my B1), attacks on an anarcho-capitalist flag and a Turkish flag called off after objections (T3-076), coordinates and gridding (T3-070), and questions on what to work on (T3-034) each have three concepts of their own: a bag.

Seven concepts hold placers to the current template: 'Stick to the template', 'Please follow the template', 'stop undoing new work', the first design finished before changing course (T3-091, both readers, my B1). The basic layout, corner coordinates and a post that 'will constantly update to direct the work' (T3-070, reader A); every reverser messaged, placers vetted through their profiles and PMed, the new plan PMed to fans keeping the old logo (T3-008); and bots 'screwing up the image', a defence script that would block the redesign, owners asked to fix their bots (T3-089) each have three concepts of their own: four themes, a bag.

A leader asked for, the moderators called on to lead, the 'admiral general' summoned and 'Pakde mah bebas~' put someone in charge (T3-101, both readers); mixed commands across too many threads with no telling which command is the last, separate threads despite the megathread, and 'where its being coordinated?' complain of scattered calls (T3-049, reader B and my B1).

'The hierarchy' names who leads Team Yellow (T3-101, both readers); 'A sign for our subreddit we could/should make' is T3-169's 'the choice whether to write it' (reader A, my B1). One concept each, two acts.

Members take the border, ask 'Someone assign me a job', are given the protective blue layer, and logo workers are moved to the blue (T3-103, both readers); 'I have no idea how to help', a guide asked for the bolt, and 'still need blue?' ask for directions (T3-034, reader B). A newcomer taught to pick blue on the palette and click, and the cooldown's drop to five minutes, are T3-016's 'how to pick a colour and place' (my B1, by the correction on teaching to place). My B1 T3-002 rests on one call.

Help asked to maintain as the Europeans go to bed, the flag handed off as North America sleeps, and a member up at 2am keep watch over the hours (T3-141, both readers). Consistent cleaning duty, 'Time to maintain!', defending on Place and maintenance asked for as the Void nears are upkeep (T3-021, reader A and my B1), primary by T3-141's decide_when_both since the shifts have concepts of their own. 'we need more help!', 'come help us out!' with the bomb, and 'STICK WITH THE DESIGN' call hands in (T3-002, reader A). Fifteen accounts made (T3-088, my B1) is one concept.

'I don't think there's any space for us now' and 'It's too late' judge the canvas full (T3-036, reader A and my B1). The opening post names a new mark, Big Bang in yellow text on black, and asks for help; by the boundary ruled once a new mark named counts toward T3-033 even when it asks for help (my B1), not T3-002 (reader B).

q: Argument or work on the mark's look: which picture or version, colours, letters, fonts, size, outlines, details; corrections to make the placed work match the design.
w: After the build, members ask whether a stranger can tell the headphone-wearing cat is Monstercat and defend it as 'the most recognizable image': whether a mark represents the room well (T3-098, reader B). One concept regrets not trying the full Shimmer artwork, 'we should've tried nonetheless': art the canvas missed (T3-148, my B1). Reader A read the same talk as T3-004's 'which picture or version', whose test does not say the design must still be open. My B1 T3-156 needs the mark taken into the sub's banner or flair, which no concept shows.

q: A choice put between fighting and moving, or between rebuilding in place and relocating: 'restore it where it was or move?', 'not this time, we fight back', a move proposed against holding on.
w: After Tails is gone, one concept calls r/Columbia to attack the Blue Corner's banner and another defends 'some measure' after Samus was wiped out (T3-006, reader B and my B1); 'Don't attack the banner, that's a lost cause. We just need to rebuild.' reins the attack in (T3-076, my B1), which T3-076's decide_when_both pairs with T3-006. The choice is attacking a rival against rebuilding in place. T3-124's must_show names fighting against moving and rebuilding against relocating, and reader A read this choice into it.

Calls to raid Chile's flag, grief Norway's, push Norway 'into submission', Operation Fuck Norway and 'a final fuck you to those Norwegian commie bastards' attack rivals' work (T3-006, both readers). 'Let us keep the space we have, assholes', 'A Texan surrendering? Ha.' and 'I say we defend' refuse to yield (T3-123, reader B). Repair first, 'Not this time. We fight back.' (T3-124's own must_show example) and 'Fix the border and let's rebuild' weigh fighting against rebuilding (T3-124, reader A and my B1). Three themes with three concepts each and no fourth. A member also shouts 'SHUT THE FUCK UP YOU COMMUNIST SNOW PEOPLE!' at the Norwegian diplomat.

All three placements hold the same three themes and differ on which leads. Questions and answers on what r/place is, one pixel every five or ten minutes, and how to click a colour and place outnumber the rest (T3-016, reader B and my B1); timer troubles handled by refreshing and checking back (T3-074, reader A first) and alts, ten accounts and private windows used to place more (T3-088) follow.
